findings_qualitative.value: Outermost CO gap at ~210 au lies beyond the mm dust edge, so it is not due to dust opacity

evidence.quote: Therefore, it cannot be explained by dust opacity and must be a real decrease in the $^{12}$CO column density at this radius.

claims.hypothesis: Can the AS 209 dust continuum be described by concentric Gaussian rings?
claims.experiment: uv-plane MCMC fit of a core plus 7 Gaussian rings
claims.result: Rings at 15, 27, 41, 74, 92, 120, 139 au with low residuals
claims.finding: Emission is well represented by narrow concentric rings, with some residual in the inner disk

evidence.quote: Our best-fit model successfully reproduces the observations, as seen by the low-level emission in the residuals map.

claims.hypothesis: Is the outer CO gap caused by dust opacity?
claims.experiment: Compare CO gaps with dust ring radii
claims.result: Gap at 210 au is beyond the dust edge
claims.finding: Requires a real CO column density reduction (chemistry or gas depletion)

evidence.quote: therefore traces real $^{12}$CO depletion or a substantial decrease in the gas density.

claims.hypothesis: Are the gaps due to snowlines or planets?
claims.experiment: Compare with snowline temperatures and hydrodynamical simulations
claims.result: Snowlines unlikely to explain all gaps; low-mass planet simulations reproduce rings

evidence.quote: it it is unlikely that all the observed gaps are induced by a chemical effect.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Snowline-induced gaps, zonal flows, dead zones judged unlikely or problematic

evidence.quote: it is hard to explain how condensation fronts alone could produce such wide gaps.
